newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB sees 50 mln stg savings from LAL.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB sees 50 mln stg savings from LAL.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc said on Monday it expected to reap cost savings of about 50 million pounds per year before tax in three years from the acquisition of the final stake in life insurer Lloyds Abbey Life (LAL).

In a statement detailing the deal announced on Friday, Lloyds TSB said it expected the purchase, that values the outstanding LAL shares at around 635 pence each, to marginally boost earnings per share in 1997, excluding synergies.
Lloyds TSB said the savings would be made through distribution, technology and adminstration of life and non-life bancassurance products as well as its hire purchase and leasing businesses.
"There will also be streamlining benefits which at this stage cannot be quanitified," the company said.

The proposal, with its simplified ownership structure creating a more flexible business, created the opportunity to cut unit cost production in the combined businesses leading to a "stronger, more competitive market position and enhanced prospects for profitable growth", Lloyds TSB said.
The deal by Britain's largest retail financial services company to buy the outstanding 37.4 percent stake in the insurance unit will cost around 1.22 billion stg, Lloyds TSB said.
Abbey Life, which is currently quoted on the stock exchange, will remain separately run and, if the deal wins shareholder approval, three independent non-executive LAL directors will leave the board.
Although the proposal would result in job cuts, Lloyds said it was aiming for voluntary redundancies and normal turnover as far as possible.
Lloyds Abbey, which posted a pretax profit of 421.5 million stg in 1995 and a first-half pretax profit of 259.2 million stg in 1996, has 1.435 billion stg of shareholder equity.
Current trading remained "satisfactory" at both LAL and Lloyds TSB, the company said.

Lloyds TSB posted a pretax profit of 2.08 billion stg in 1995 before a 425 million stg restructuring charge. Half year pretax profits in 1996 came in at 1.14 billion stg with shareholders' equity standing at 4.79 billion stg.
Under the deal, minority LAL investors will get six Lloyds TSB shares and 2,100 pence cash for every seven LAL shares.
Of the cash, 350 pence net -- 50 pence net per share -- will be by way of a special dividend from Lloyds Abbey.
